unit_rules: Counts refer to people unless explicitly described otherwise.
A foot, photograph, timepoint, assay, paper or press release is not an independent clinical participant.
Null means not established, not zero.
Do not sum active-treated values across sequential oral/topical regimens, duplicated reports or mixed routes.
Do not calculate a pooled response proportion or Phase II-success probability from this ledger.

count_summary.comment: Oral and topical totals overlap through Greco patients; SGT studies have differing diseases and arm denominators and are not added.

searched_sources: Primary journal full text and conference abstracts
Indexed ANZCTR, WHO and Israeli registry domains

erlotinib AND (topical OR ointment OR gel)

studies.title: Lee and Lowe: KRT16 palmoplantar keratoderma
studies.population: Hereditary KRT16 c.379C>T p.Arg127Cys palmoplantar keratoderma
studies.design: Two cases with randomized double-blind opposite-foot periods and uncontrolled bilateral extensions
studies.source_access: Full two-page primary PDF read; direct URL intermittently fails; indexed full copy accessible. Later conference abstract read.
studies.observed_claim: Local morphological improvement during controlled 1% periods; marked pain/function improvement in mother during open bilateral treatment.
limitations: One related pair; neither feet nor repeated periods are independent patients.
No numeric placebo-foot pain series or paired treatment effect, variance, registration, protocol or randomization method.
Published phase durations and figure labels disagree.
Exact compounded formulation, applied mass, later application frequencies, skin exposure and systemic PK missing.
No complete AE ascertainment or denominator of all patients considered.
duplicate_reports: 10.1111/ajd.14044 conference abstract: same mother-son cases; not additional patients

baseline.analgesic: Daily tapentadol; subsequent cessation not documented

phases.design: Randomized double-blind opposite-foot; unblinded at week 6

phases.treatment: 0.1% erlotinib with 10% salicylic acid cream twice weekly

phases.result: Active foot improved morphologically; active-foot pain 0-3/10; numeric control pain absent

phases.treatment: 1% ointment and keratolytic to both feet
phases.result: Pain-free soles, free ambulation, swimming; palmar improvement also reported

patients.timing_discrepancy: 6+12 implies week18, whereas third photograph is week20. No explanation supplied.
patients.harms: No adverse effects reported over 60 weeks; structured AE surveillance not described

phases.treatment: 1% ointment left foot and 10% salicylic acid cream; poor keratolytic adherence
phases.control: Placebo right foot with prescribed keratolytic
phases.result: Modest active-foot morphological improvement; numeric pain absent

phases.treatment: 1% ointment both feet; limited keratolytic use

patients.timing_discrepancy: Prose 12 + 12 weeks and 24-week safety differ from last photograph at 28 weeks; later meeting abstract 26 weeks.
patients.harms: No adverse effects reported over 24 weeks

studies.decision_role: Exact-genotype efficacy hypothesis; insufficient for an effect-size or Phase II-success estimate

studies.title: Greco et al.: topical then systemic EGFR inhibition
studies.population: Keratin-associated PPK classified as PC by authors
studies.design: Two-person prospective intervention, not registered as clinical trial; one uncontrolled oral-to-topical switch and one treated-versus-untreated foot comparison
studies.observed_claim: 0.2% cream did not provide adequate sustained control; one person had a partial early foot-pain benefit. Oral treatment provided more benefit but produced dose-limiting skin effects.
limitations: Different formulation, alleles and background treatment from Lee.
Neither topical phase was blinded vehicle-controlled.
No LLOQ for reported undetectable topical erlotinib blood concentration.
Low concentration as cause of inadequate benefit is a hypothesis.

patients.phenotype: Focal PPK without dystrophic nails, oral leukokeratosis, follicular hyperkeratosis or cysts
patients.topical: 0.2% oil-in-water cream,1 g/foot twice daily after stopping oral 75 mg/day
patients.topical_result: Slower plaque regrowth but major pain recurrence; resumed oral
patients.oral: 75 mg/day initially;100 mg/day produced painful acral cracks; later changed to lapatinib
patients.oral_harms: Acneiform eruption and painful fissures with dose escalation

patients.phenotype: Focal PPK, nail dystrophy, oral leukokeratosis and follicular hyperkeratosis
patients.topical: 0.2% oil-in-water cream,1 g right foot twice daily;left untreated
patients.topical_result: At 1 month NRS 4 right versus 7 left; improved debridement but still 2-3 times/month; later plateau prompted oral
patients.topical_pk: Residual blood concentration undetectable; LLOQ absent
patients.oral: 75 mg/day; interrupted after acneiform rash; resumed 25 mg/day
patients.oral_result: Pain and walking improved at lower dose

studies.decision_role: Direct contrary/partial topical evidence; exposure and tolerability warning

studies.title: SGT-84-01 PPK proof of concept
studies.population: Launch specified punctate palmoplantar keratoderma type 1; participant genotypes not published
studies.source_access: Primary issuer launch/results and SEC narrative read; full trial report/protocol not recovered.
studies.observed_claim: Issuer reported modest improvement and favorable safety at a very low concentration.
limitations: Six completed does not specify active-arm exposure or all enrolled.
Approximately 15 was a target, not observed enrollment.
No arm-level efficacy, strength, participant flow, full harms or genotype table recovered.
Later filings say Q3 2021 although June 28 release already discloses results.
Punctate PPK type 1 is not interchangeable with Lee KRT16 disease.
studies.decision_role: Independent topical clinical experience; modest, poorly quantified result

studies.title: SGT-210 maximal-use PK healthy-volunteer study
studies.design: Single-center, single-blind, parallel two-strength maximal-use study; 12 participants randomized 1:1
studies.source_access: Issuer SEC summary read; patent Example 13 independently verified in companion product audit; PC Project public update supplies matching 12-subject, 28-day lineage.
studies.observed_claim: 3.5% and 5% ointments,28days; issuer reports tolerance and low systemic absorption; patent reports values below assay quantification.
limitations: Not an efficacy study or diseased-plantar-skin exposure study.
Finite LLOQs, not zero absorption; no inferable exposure-response estimate.
Short duration and different product/population from Lee.

exposure.pk_analysis: Not conducted because concentrations below quantification

studies.harms: Issuer: most drug-related events mild, all resolved; no safety findings affecting adherence; full AE table not recovered in human audit
studies.decision_role: Product-specific short-term tolerability and assay-bounded PK

studies.title: SGT-210 Darier Phase 1b Stage 1
studies.design: Vehicle-controlled phase1b; stage1 ended after recruitment difficulties; open-label extension was planned
studies.source_access: Primary issuer/SEC reports read; raw arm-level data not recovered.
studies.observed_claim: No differentiation on efficacy assessments after unblinding; sponsor decided not to advance Darier indication.
limitations: November wording describes seven enrolled completers, without clear total screened/enrolled/active-treated denominators.
No exact arm sizes, effects, endpoints, confidence intervals or genotype table recovered.
Negative result in different disease does not establish KRT16 futility or equivalence.
studies.decision_role: Material topical negative evidence and concrete rare-disease recruitment warning

studies.title: SGT-210 pediatric compassionate case
studies.population: Pediatric Olmsted syndrome; genotype not disclosed
studies.source_access: Primary issuer updates read; peer-reviewed case report not found.
studies.observed_claim: Improvement in facial and hand hyperkeratosis, pain and itching reported by issuer.
limitations: Age, genotype, strength, mass, duration, baseline, standardized outcomes and harms absent.
Different phenotype/anatomic sites from painful KRT16 plantar disease.
Repeated updates are one case; requests for use in other conditions are not treated participants.

studies.title: Basset et al.: EGFR signaling and oral PC treatment
studies.population: Genetically defined PC: KRT16 and KRT6A
studies.design: Three treated cases from two pedigrees;fourth participant contributes disease material but not treatment
studies.source_access: Full primary paper and supplementary clinical table read; earlier symposium summary read.
studies.observed_claim: Uncontrolled pain, function and quality-of-life improvements with daily oral erlotinib.
limitations: No vehicle/control arm or blinded assessment.
Patient-reported foot-function index is not an objective ambulatory measure or PC-specific endpoint validation.
Timepoints and bilateral feet are not additional patients.
Does not establish topical delivery or benefit.
studies.harms: Moderate acneiform lesions inP1 and P3; topical 5% benzoyl peroxide and oral doxycycline100 mg/day forP3 used
studies.decision_role: Independent oral pharmacology and endpoint precedent; not topical replication

studies.title: BJD O16: Erlotinib in pachyonychia congenita
studies.population: PC anecdotes; one KRT16 pre/post callus
studies.design: Mechanistic cell/callus abstract with background clinical anecdotes
studies.source_access: Full abstract read; no individual clinical ledger supplied.
studies.observed_claim: Mentions anecdotal clinical benefit in six patients and analyzes one pre/post-treatment callus sample.
limitations: Route and individual clinical histories insufficiently specified.
Six cannot be added to earlier case series without linkage.
Not a six-person controlled clinical study.
studies.decision_role: Mechanistic support and lead for later data diligence; excluded from independent efficacy count

studies.title: Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Inhibition for Keratinopathies
studies.population: Adults with PC, epidermolytic ichthyosis or specified PPK
studies.design: Open-label single-arm Phase 1/2; 8-week baseline; 24-week escalation 50/75/100 mg; extension
studies.source_access: Primary ClinicalTrials.gov API retrieved directly on 9 November 2026.
studies.observed_claim: Not yet recruiting; no posted results.
limitations: 44 is estimated enrollment, not observed participants.
Oral, mixed genotypes, open-label; not topical randomized evidence.
studies.decision_role: Future evidence and recruitment context; no efficacy contribution

studies.title: Recent oral Olmsted reports: source-access ledger
studies.source_access: PMID 40615090 bibliographic record, no abstract/full clinical tables recovered; PMID 41362860 title/metadata; PMID 40859917 metadata; 2026 pediatric combination primary text indexed and read; 2025 CED primary case excerpt read.
studies.observed_claim: Additional human oral experience exists, including combination treatment. No aggregate efficacy estimate extracted.
limitations: Do not infer positive findings from bibliographic titles alone.
Individual deduplication incomplete across oral Olmsted literature.
Combination treatment cannot isolate erlotinib contribution.
2026 pediatric paper intro saysstart age 5 while case text says 4.
studies.decision_role: Transportability context and disclosed access limits; no topical efficacy count
